text.p: Dollar/mark will remain bullish after the Fourth of July weekend and may take out the 1994 high of 1.7686, analysts said on Thursday.
At 1700 GMT, the dollar was quoted at 1.7515/25 marks versus 1.7535/45 at the open, and at 113.50/60 yen vs. 114.31/36. Earlier in the session, dollar/mark set a fresh 40-month high at 1.7566

Technicians said dollar/mark retained a lot of momentum despite some expected profit-taking ahead of the extended Fourth of July weekend. U.S. markets will be closed on Friday for the national holiday. Trading will resume on Monday.

"We tested the downside at 1.7465 whose loss could have signaled a deeper correction but it held," said senior analyst Scott Siller at CurrencyWatch, referring to the dollar/mark low on Wednesday and Thursday.
Siller, however, said the dollar/mark downside was limited, with strong support at 1.7410 and 1.7355, while "1.7310 would surely represent a good buying opportunity."

Chartists said dollar/mark posted four 40-month highs in four days and closed higher for six straight sessions which signaled enough momentum to take out a critical level, the 1994 high of 1.7686 set on February 8.

Chartists said there were few significant levels on the way to 1.7686, with 1.76 as the only intermediate resistance, while, past 1.7686, the next highs date back to August 1991 with a peak of 1.8350.
Technicians said a big level on the way would be 1.7790, the 62-percent retracement of the slide from the 2.0478 high in June 1989 to the record low of 1.3438, on March 8, 1995.
The mark's weakness was most evident versus sterling which roared to a fresh near-six-year high at 2.9605 and versus the yen where a key psychological support at 65.00 gave way.
"Mark/yen is just a horror show," MCM's Siller said.

I.D.E.A. analyst Ben Morden said sterling/mark has an objective at 3.00 which would be accompanied by 1.77 on dollar/mark and $1.70 for cable. Likewise, mark/yen weakness is expected to weigh further on dollar/yen -- holding less than one yen above very strong support at 112.85.
On the upside, 115.30 remains an important level for dollar/yen on the way to 117.00, the 38-percent retracement of the 1997 high-low move from 127.47 on May 1 to 110.62 June 11.
Dollar/Swiss has been bullish since taking out 1.4660, a key level on a rising trendline targeting 1.4922, the retest of the March 6 high.
